sections.html:
The Caswell County Tax Office takes listings, exemption forms and bill payments from the courthouse at 139 E. Church Street, Yanceyville. Write to PO Box 204, Yanceyville, NC 27379, or call (336) 694-4194 ext. 5116. Hours are eight to five on weekdays.

Cards can be used through an outside payment service, with a fee that rises along with the tax amount. Bill numbers begin with R for real estate or P for personal property, and you leave off the zero that follows the letter when you type the number in. The county home page has a Pay A Tax Bill link to an online bill search.

Two other offices matter when you sell. The Register of Deeds is downstairs in the same courthouse complex at (336) 694-4197. The county GIS office, at (336) 694-4194 ext. 115, matches parcels to maps. If a bill is still open, call the tax office first for a payoff on the parcel.

The county rate is 62.7 cents per $100 of value for property listed as of January 1, 2025. The county was last reappraised effective January 1, 2024, and the next countywide reappraisal is scheduled for 2028.

Ten fire districts exist: Anderson, Casville, Cherry Grove, Leasburg, Milton, Pelham, Prospect Hill, Providence, Semora and Yanceyville. Which one covers your house depends on the parcel, so ask the tax office for the exact combined charge at an address.

For the current year's rate, call the tax office or open the budget ordinance on the county home page.

Value disputes go to the county's board of equalization and review. Ask the tax office for the board's meeting dates and appeal form ahead of the spring session. The calendar comes from state law:

  • The board's opening session lands somewhere from the first April Monday to the first May Monday.
  • Outside a reappraisal year the board wraps up about three Mondays after opening and generally stops by July 1. In a reappraisal year it has until December 1.
  • Request a hearing before adjournment, in writing or by showing up. A decision notice mailed late in the session extends your window by 15 days from the mailing.
  • Its written decision is mailed within 30 days after it adjourns.
  • Still unhappy? Mail a written notice of appeal to the Property Tax Commission within 30 days of the board's decision date, copying the county assessor.

Because the 2024 reappraisal is the latest, the next large wave of appeals is tied to 2028. In between, a value usually moves only after a physical change to the property, a clerical error or a change in permitted use, so a quiet-year appeal should name one of those.

The state's January 1, 2025 sales ratio study showed a median ratio of 104.97 for the county. If your value looks high, gather recent nearby sales of comparable houses and dated photos of defects present on January 1.

Three state homestead programs exist, and an owner can use only one. Applications use Form AV-9 and go to the county tax office, which must accept them up to June 1 before the tax year.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shelters half of a home's appraised value or $25,000, whichever is larger, for an owner who is 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled and whose prior-year income is under the cap. The 2026 cap is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: waives $45,000 of appraised value whatever the applicant's age or income. Form NCDVA-9 is filled out with a county veteran service officer first.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: caps the bill at 4 percent of income for owners under the cap and 5 percent for those up to 150 percent of it ($58,200 for 2026). The owner reapplies every year.

Sellers should know the catch with the circuit breaker: the deferred amount is a lien, and a transfer makes the previous three fiscal years' deferrals payable. A house that used the deferment carries an extra payoff on the closing statement.

The tax office page links the state's exemption, exclusion and present-use value forms, as well as business personal property listing forms.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill at a sale?
sections.html:
The tax stays with the land, so an open balance is paid out of the sale at closing. The statutory lien for a given year takes hold on January 1, the listing date, along with later penalties, interest and costs.

A bill is due September 1 and costs face value until January 6. Interest then begins at 2 percent for the balance of January, followed by three-fourths of a percent for each month or part of one. A seller with an open prior-year bill takes those charges to the closing table.

The deed adds its own charges. The seller pays the state's conveyance excise tax, $1.00 per $500 of price or fraction, to the register of deeds before recording. Recording fees are fixed by statute: $26 for an ordinary instrument's first 15 pages and $64 for a deed of trust's first 35.

If a bill stays unpaid for long, the county may sue to foreclose the tax lien the way a lender would foreclose a mortgage, and the parcel goes to auction at the courthouse door. Redemption stays open until confirmation, on payment of what is owed. Selling first is the cleaner route.

Caswell County is thinly settled, with 53.5 people per square mile in 2020. Yanceyville is the seat, and Milton is the other town named on the county website. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 22,563 residents, down 0.8 percent from the 2020 base.

Homes are inexpensive here. The 2020-2024 median for owned homes is $164,500, with owners living in 75.2 percent of them. About a quarter of residents, 25.4 percent, are 65 or older, an age group the elderly exclusion is built for.

County Environmental Health handles private septic permits, so a seller with a septic system can ask that office for the records on file.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Caswell County tax office?
faqs.a: Call (336) 694-4194 ext. 5116. The office is at 139 E. Church Street in Yanceyville, open Monday through Friday, eight to five. Keep your bill number handy and drop the zero after the R or P.

faqs.q: What is the Caswell County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The 2025-26 rate is 62.7 cents on each $100 of property listed as of January 1, 2025. Fire district tax adds 3.3 cents in the Casville and County Fire Service districts, and solid waste fees are $55 and $75. For the current year, ask the tax office.

faqs.q: When is the next Caswell County revaluation?
faqs.a: The schedule shows 2028, following the reappraisal effective January 1, 2024. Counties must reappraise at least every eighth year and may choose shorter cycles. Confirm the date with the tax office, since schedules can move.

faqs.q: When are Caswell County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. Paying before January 6 of the next year costs face value, and from that day interest starts at 2 percent, moving to three-fourths of a percent monthly. A mailed payment counts on its postmark date.

faqs.q: Is a sale possible with Caswell County tax still owed?
faqs.a: Yes. Whatever is open, interest included, comes out of your proceeds at the closing table. Request a payoff figure from the tax office before choosing a closing date, and ask if a circuit breaker deferral adds a second balance.
